items.name: Neuroscience or biopsychological perspective
items.plain_en: studies psychology from a biological viewpoint

items.name: Genetic predisposition
items.plain_en: inherited tendency toward a trait or condition

items.name: DNA
items.plain_en: chromosome material holding genetic information

items.name: Genes
items.plain_en: DNA segments controlling specific protein production

items.name: Dominant or recessive genes
items.plain_en: dominant expressed with one copy; recessive two

items.name: Identical twins (monozygotic twins)
items.plain_en: twins from one fertilized egg sharing all genes

items.name: Chromosomal abnormality
items.plain_en: unusual chromosome combination or number

items.name: Turner’s syndrome
items.plain_en: born with only one X chromosome

items.name: Klinefelter’s syndrome
items.plain_en: extra X chromosome producing XXY pattern

items.name: Down syndrome
items.plain_en: extra chromosome on chromosome pair 21

items.name: Neuroanatomy
items.plain_en: study of neuron parts and functions

items.name: Neurons
items.plain_en: individual nerve cells

items.name: Dendrites
items.plain_en: rootlike branches extending from cell body

items.name: Cell body (soma)
items.plain_en: neuron's main part containing the nucleus

items.name: Axon
items.plain_en: wirelike structure extending from the cell body

items.name: Myelin sheath
items.plain_en: fatty covering around axon, speeds impulses

items.name: Terminal buttons
items.plain_en: branched axon ends containing neurotransmitters

items.name: Synapse
items.plain_en: space between terminal buttons and next dendrites

items.name: Neurotransmitters
items.plain_en: chemicals enabling communication between neurons

items.name: Resting potential
items.plain_en: slightly negative neuron charge at rest

items.name: Threshold
items.plain_en: stimulation level required to trigger firing

items.name: Action potential
items.plain_en: electric impulse traveling along the neuron

items.name: All-or-none principle
items.plain_en: neuron either fires completely or not at all

items.name: Depolarization
items.plain_en: positive ions entering make charge positive

items.name: Excitatory neurotransmitters
items.plain_en: neurotransmitters that excite the next cell

items.name: Inhibitory neurotransmitters
items.plain_en: neurotransmitters that inhibit the next cell

items.name: Sensory neurons (afferent neurons)
items.plain_en: carry sensory information from senses to brain

items.name: Interneurons (association neurons)
items.plain_en: connect sensory and motor neurons within CNS

items.name: Motor neurons (efferent neurons)
items.plain_en: carry information from brain to body

items.name: Organization of the Nervous System
items.plain_en: two divisions: central and peripheral nervous systems

items.name: Central nervous system (CNS)
items.plain_en: brain and spinal cord

items.name: Spinal cord
items.plain_en: nerve bundle running through center of spine

items.name: Afferent nerves
items.plain_en: nerves carrying sensory messages toward CNS

items.name: Reflex arcs
items.plain_en: involuntary reactions handled by the spinal cord

items.name: Peripheral nervous system (PNS)
items.plain_en: nerves outside CNS, not encased in bone

items.name: Somatic nervous system
items.plain_en: controls voluntary muscle movements

items.name: Autonomic nervous system
items.plain_en: controls automatic functions like heart and organs

items.name: Fight-or-flight response
items.plain_en: body prepares to respond to perceived threat

items.name: Sympathetic nervous system
items.plain_en: mobilizes body to respond to stress

items.name: Parasympathetic nervous system
items.plain_en: calms body, returns it to homeostasis

items.name: Endocrine system
items.plain_en: glands secreting hormones affecting body processes

items.name: Adrenal glands
items.plain_en: produce adrenaline preparing body for fight or flight

items.name: Ovaries and testes
items.plain_en: produce sex hormones estrogen and testosterone

items.name: Ways of Studying the Brain
items.plain_en: methods for detecting brain function

items.name: Accidents
items.plain_en: brain injuries give clues about function

items.name: Phineas Gage
items.plain_en: brain injury changed his emotions and impulses

items.name: Lesioning
items.plain_en: destroying or removing brain tissue

items.name: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
items.plain_en: detects and records brain waves

items.name: Computerized axial tomography (CAT or CT) scan
items.plain_en: sophisticated X-ray image of brain

items.name: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
items.plain_en: magnetic scan producing detailed brain images

items.name: Positron emission tomography (PET) scan
items.plain_en: shows brain areas active during tasks

items.name: Functional MRI (fMRI)
items.plain_en: combines MRI and PET scan elements

items.name: Brain Structure and Function
items.plain_en: brain's three sections: hindbrain, midbrain, forebrain

items.name: Hindbrain
items.plain_en: life support; controls basic biological functions

items.name: Medulla
items.plain_en: controls blood pressure, heart rate, breathing

items.name: Pons
items.plain_en: connects hindbrain with midbrain and forebrain

items.name: Cerebellum
items.plain_en: coordinates habitual muscle movements

items.name: Midbrain
items.plain_en: coordinates simple movements with sensory information

items.name: Reticular formation
items.plain_en: netlike cells controlling arousal and attention

items.name: Forebrain
items.plain_en: brain areas controlling thought and reasoning

items.name: Thalamus
items.plain_en: relays sensory signals to appropriate forebrain areas

items.name: Hypothalamus
items.plain_en: regulates temperature, hunger, thirst, and endocrine system

items.name: Amygdala and hippocampus
items.plain_en: amygdala handles emotion; hippocampus handles memory

items.name: Limbic system
items.plain_en: group of emotion and memory regions

items.name: Cerebral cortex
items.plain_en: thin gray wrinkled layer of neurons

items.name: Pruning
items.plain_en: trimming neural connections into complex networks

items.name: Hemispheres
items.plain_en: cortex divided into left and right halves

items.name: Contralateral hemispheric organization
items.plain_en: each brain side controls the opposite body side

items.name: Hemispheric specialization (brain lateralization)
items.plain_en: each hemisphere specializes in different functions

items.name: Split-brain patients
items.plain_en: patients whose corpus callosum was cut

items.name: Association area
items.plain_en: cortex areas neither sensory nor motor

items.name: Frontal lobes
items.plain_en: cortex at top front of brain

items.name: Prefrontal cortex
items.plain_en: directs thought, planning, and emotional control

items.name: Broca’s area
items.plain_en: controls muscles producing speech

items.name: Motor cortex
items.plain_en: sends signals controlling voluntary movements

items.name: Parietal lobes
items.plain_en: cortex behind frontal lobe, top of brain

items.name: Somatosensory cortex
items.plain_en: receives touch information from the body

items.name: Phantom limb syndrome
items.plain_en: sensations perceived from missing body part

items.name: Occipital lobes
items.plain_en: back of brain; interprets visual messages

items.name: Temporal lobes
items.plain_en: process sound sensed by ears

items.name: Wernicke’s area
items.plain_en: language processing for written and spoken speech

items.name: Brain plasticity
items.plain_en: brain flexibility to reorganize after damage

items.name: Consciousness
items.plain_en: awareness of one's own mental state

items.name: Mere exposure effect
items.plain_en: prefer familiar stimuli over novel ones

items.name: Priming
items.plain_en: prior exposure speeds later responses

items.name: Blind sight
items.plain_en: blind people accurately sense unseen objects

items.name: Conscious level
items.plain_en: information currently within awareness

items.name: Nonconscious level
items.plain_en: body processes outside our awareness

items.name: Preconscious level
items.plain_en: information retrievable into conscious awareness

items.name: Subconscious level
items.plain_en: unaware information inferred from behavior

items.name: Unconscious level
items.plain_en: repressed unacceptable feelings and events

items.name: Psychoactive drugs
items.plain_en: chemicals changing brain chemistry and consciousness

items.name: Blood-brain barrier
items.plain_en: protects brain from harmful blood chemicals

items.name: Agonists
items.plain_en: drugs mimicking neurotransmitter effects

items.name: Antagonists
items.plain_en: drugs blocking neurotransmitter effects

items.name: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
items.plain_en: prevents serotonin reabsorption back into neuron

items.name: Tolerance
items.plain_en: need more drug for same effect

items.name: Withdrawal symptoms
items.plain_en: uncomfortable effects after stopping drug use

items.name: Psychological dependence
items.plain_en: intense psychological desire or craving

items.name: Physical dependence
items.plain_en: body needs drug to avoid withdrawal

items.name: Stimulants
items.plain_en: speed up body processes and heart rate

items.name: Depressants
items.plain_en: slow down body systems

items.name: Hallucinogens
items.plain_en: cause perceptual changes and hallucinations

items.name: Reverse tolerance
items.plain_en: smaller doses cause same or stronger effects

items.name: Opiates
items.plain_en: endorphin agonists; powerful painkillers and mood elevators

items.name: Sleep deprived
items.plain_en: not getting as much sleep as needed

items.name: Circadian rhythm
items.plain_en: roughly 24-hour biological rhythm

items.name: Sleep cycle
items.plain_en: typical pattern of sleep stages

items.name: Sleep onset
items.plain_en: period of falling asleep

items.name: Alpha waves
items.plain_en: brain waves when drowsy but awake

items.name: Theta waves
items.plain_en: high-frequency, low-amplitude waves in NREM 1 and 2

items.name: Sleep spindles
items.plain_en: short bursts of rapid brain waves

items.name: Delta sleep
items.plain_en: deep slow-wave sleep with delta waves

items.name: Restoration of resources
items.plain_en: sleep rebuilds resources used while awake

items.name: REM sleep
items.plain_en: rapid eye movement; brain waves appear active

items.name: REM rebound
items.plain_en: more REM after REM deprivation

items.name: Insomnia
items.plain_en: persistent trouble falling or staying asleep

items.name: Narcolepsy
items.plain_en: intense sleepiness; falls asleep at inappropriate times

items.name: Sleep apnea
items.plain_en: breathing stops briefly during the night

items.name: Night terrors
items.plain_en: children wake from terror, remember nothing

items.name: Somnambulism (sleepwalking)
items.plain_en: walking while asleep

items.name: Dreams
items.plain_en: storylike images experienced during sleep

items.name: Lucid dreams
items.plain_en: aware of dreaming and controlling storyline

items.name: Activation-synthesis theory of dreaming
items.plain_en: dreams interpret physiological brain activity during REM

items.name: Information-processing theory of dreaming
items.plain_en: dreams process events of the day

items.name: Consolidation theory of dreams
items.plain_en: dreams help consolidate short-term into long-term memory

items.name: Sensation
items.plain_en: activation of the senses

items.name: Perception
items.plain_en: process of understanding sensations

items.name: Transduction
items.plain_en: signals transformed into neural impulses

items.name: Sensory adaptation
items.plain_en: decreasing responsiveness to constant stimulation

items.name: Sensory habituation
items.plain_en: perception depends partly on attention focus

items.name: Cocktail party effect
items.plain_en: involuntarily notice your name across the room

items.name: Synesthesia
items.plain_en: one sense activates another sense

items.name: Prosopagnosia
items.plain_en: inability to recognize faces

items.name: Vision
items.plain_en: dominant human sense

items.name: Retina
items.plain_en: screen at the back of the eye

items.name: Hues
items.plain_en: different wavelengths appear as different hues

items.name: Amplitude
items.plain_en: wave height determines intensity

items.name: Cornea
items.plain_en: eye's first structure light passes through

items.name: Pupil
items.plain_en: opening controlling amount of light entering

items.name: Accommodation
items.plain_en: lens changes shape to focus light

items.name: Transduction
items.plain_en: stimuli translated into neural signals

items.name: Cones
items.plain_en: retina cells activated by color

items.name: Rods
items.plain_en: cells responding to black and white

items.name: Fovea
items.plain_en: retina center with highest cone concentration

items.name: Blind spot
items.plain_en: no receptors where optic nerve exits

items.name: Optic chiasm
items.plain_en: where optic nerves cross

items.name: Feature detectors
items.plain_en: neurons responding to specific visual features

items.name: Theories of color vision
items.plain_en: competing explanations of color perception

items.name: Trichromatic theory
items.plain_en: three cone types detect red, green, blue

items.name: Afterimage
items.plain_en: complementary color seen after staring

items.name: Dichromatism
items.plain_en: cannot see red-green or blue-yellow shades

items.name: Opponent-process theory
items.plain_en: color receptors arranged in opposing pairs

items.name: Pitch
items.plain_en: wave frequency determines pitch

items.name: Loudness
items.plain_en: wave amplitude determines loudness

items.name: Cochlea
items.plain_en: snail-shaped fluid-filled inner ear structure

items.name: Sound localization
items.plain_en: judging where a sound originated

items.name: Pitch theories
items.plain_en: two theories explaining pitch perception

items.name: Place theory
items.plain_en: hair cells respond based on location

items.name: Frequency theory
items.plain_en: hair cells fire at different rates

items.name: Conduction deafness
items.plain_en: sound conduction pathway is damaged

items.name: Nerve deafness
items.plain_en: damaged cochlear hair cells cause deafness

items.name: Gate control theory
items.plain_en: some pain messages have higher priority

items.name: Pain receptors
items.plain_en: nerve endings firing with sharp stimulation

items.name: Endorphins
items.plain_en: natural pain-killing chemicals in the body

items.name: Taste buds
items.plain_en: tongue structures absorbing food chemicals

items.name: Papillae
items.plain_en: visible bumps on the tongue

items.name: Five different types of tastes
items.plain_en: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami, fat

items.name: Supertasters
items.plain_en: densely packed taste buds, intense taste

items.name: Smell (or Olfaction)
items.plain_en: depends on chemicals emitted by substances

items.name: Olfactory bulb
items.plain_en: gathers smell messages, sends to brain

items.name: Vestibular sense
items.plain_en: body orientation in space

items.name: Semicircular canals
items.plain_en: inner ear canals giving orientation feedback

items.name: Kinesthetic sense (kinesthesis)
items.plain_en: position and movement of specific body parts
